episodeTitle.en: Thinking like a gardener, slime mold, the adjacent possible: Product advice from Alex Komoroske
episodeTitle.zh: 像园丁一样思考、黏菌、邻近可能性：亚历克斯·科莫罗斯基的产品建议

guestBioOfficial.en: Alex Komoroske is a strategic leader who merges the practice, theory, and mindset necessary to tackle complex problems. He spent 13 years at Google, where he worked on Search and DoubleClick and led Chrome’s Open Web Platform. He also spearheaded Augmented Reality in Google Maps and developed toolkits to align companywide strategy from the ground up. After serving as Head of Corporate Strategy at Stripe, he is now co-founding a startup aimed at reimagining the web for the AI era. Alex created the popular “Slime Molds” deck, which offers fresh insights into organizational dynamics. He is also the author of the widely read “Bits and Bobs,” a collection of thought-provoking reflections.In our conversation, we delve into: • “Organizational kayfabe”
guestBioOfficial.zh: 亚历克斯·科莫罗斯基是一位战略领袖，他融合了应对复杂问题所需的实践、理论和思维模式。他曾在谷歌工作 13 年，先后负责搜索和 DoubleClick 项目，并领导 Chrome 的开放网络平台。他还主导了谷歌地图中的增强现实功能开发，并开发了从零开始构建全公司战略的工具包。在担任 Stripe 企业战略主管后，他目前正与人共同创办一家旨在为人工智能时代重新构想网络的初创公司。亚历克斯创作了广受欢迎的《黏菌》演示文稿，为组织动态提供了全新的洞见。他还是广受欢迎的《零零碎碎》系列文章的作者，该系列文集充满了发人深省的思考。在我们的对话中，我们将深入探讨：• “组织内的‘kayfabe’现象”

title.en: Thinking like a gardener, slime mold, the adjacent possible: Product advice from Alex Komoroske
title.zh: 像园丁一样思考、黏菌、邻近可能性：亚历克斯·科莫罗斯基的产品建议

summary.en: Alex makes the case for thinking like a gardener rather than a builder—cultivating systems that grow and compound on their own instead of forcing a fixed plan. He explores how LLMs and generative AI will reshape product building, which skills will matter most, and what organizations can learn from slime mold and “the adjacent possible.” The conversation ranges across strategy salons, organizational kayfabe, and why directing emergent behavior beats brute-force control.
summary.zh: Alex 主张像“园丁”而非“建造者”一样思考——培育能自主生长、自我复合的系统，而不是强推既定计划。他探讨了 LLM 和生成式 AI 将如何重塑产品构建、未来哪些技能最关键，以及组织能从黏菌和“邻近可能”中学到什么。对话还涵盖策略沙龙、组织性的 kayfabe，以及为何引导涌现行为优于蛮力控制。
